scope: Two exact pending P0 leaves. No production article, mapping, index or report modified. This package is not bilingual publication content and does not complete coverage.

selection.method: Read pending P0 meningitis/stroke categories and all fourteen Chinese sections of existing canonical articles; confirm exact leaf metadata against batch scope review.

sources.locator: What it is; Symptoms / When to seek emergency care; Risk factors; Prevention; Treatment and recovery (browser extraction lines 32-124)
sources.population_region: US general public; children, young infants, immunocompromised people explicitly discussed
sources.supports: Non-polio enteroviruses are common US causes; suspected meningitis needs prompt assessment; mild viral cases often recover, whereas severe/high-risk cases may need admission. Antiviral benefits described for selected other viruses must not be transferred to enterovirus.
sources.limits: A viral-meningitis overview, not a neonatal or enteroviral meningitis treatment guideline; its recovery interval is not permission to wait before assessment.
sources.upstream: No full primary-study bibliography shown in the inspected article. CDC family pages are not independent guideline groups.

sources.access_status: opened; full clinical factsheet text read
sources.locator: What are enteroviruses?; How is it spread?; Who is at risk?; How is it diagnosed?; How is it treated?; Signs of a serious infection; Outbreaks (lines 27-96)
sources.population_region: Australia/NSW; mainly children but adults can have enteroviral meningitis
sources.supports: Secretions, stool and contaminated hands/surfaces transmit enteroviruses; CSF and other samples may be tested; management is supportive. Young infants merit particular care. Deterioration warrants urgent reassessment even after earlier examination.
sources.limits: Old factsheet: vaccine availability and notification rules are local and time-sensitive. Do not export them worldwide. General enterovirus infection does not establish CNS infection.
sources.upstream: Separately authored state health factsheet; no study bibliography proving statistical independence. Its content is a stated upstream source for healthdirect.

sources.access_status: opened; patient article and Sources read
sources.supports: Patient-facing hydration, symptom relief and hygiene wording can inform style after meningitis-specific clinical review.
sources.limits: Not counted as a third independent corroborator: explicitly cites NSW Health and CDC. Its broad enterovirus page includes a parechovirus reference; do not transfer that taxonomy into this exact ICD leaf.
sources.upstream: NSW Health Enteroviruses fact sheet; CDC Non-Polio Enteroviruses, explicitly listed at Sources.

sources.institution: US CDC / Division of Bacterial Diseases
sources.access_status: opened; clinical overview text and references read
sources.locator: Cause; Types; Risk factors; Prevention; Diagnosis; Complications (lines 31-124); references (141-143)
sources.supports: H. influenzae includes encapsulated a-f and nontypeable strains. Serotyping informs public-health action. Hib vaccination does not cover non-b disease. Secondary non-b transmission is possible, especially in vulnerable people.
sources.limits: Acute treatment is delegated to AAP Red Book, which was not opened. Therefore no antimicrobial regimen or dose is validated here.
sources.upstream: Oliver et al., MMWR 2023 secondary disease study; Blain et al., OFID 2014 older adult disease. Links to CDC ACIP are the same institution, not an independent author group.

sources.access_status: initial HTML open successful; summary, introduction and evidence sections through line 141 read; subsequent offset opens timed out
sources.locator: Summary of changes (81-86); Introduction (87-98); Risk of secondary cases (123-131); Eradication of carriage (132-141)
sources.population_region: UK confirmed invasive Hib cases and contacts; not all H. influenzae serotypes
sources.supports: 2024 policy offers prophylaxis to confirmed invasive Hib cases and all household contacts. Policy changed from the prior vulnerable-household criterion. Contact evidence is heavily based on older pre-vaccine US studies; present-day UK epidemiology shaped the recommendation.
sources.limits: Detailed downstream regimen sections were not successfully read; do not infer drug dose, timing or exceptions from this package. UK policy is not a universal contact rule.
sources.upstream: Older US household transmission/carriage studies overlap the field informing ACIP; two independent institutions do not mean independent trials. Exact bibliography intersection not established.

sources.version: 2014 MMWR Recommendations and Reports 63(RR-01); linked by 2025 CDC clinical overview
sources.access_status: opened; methods, background and chemoprophylaxis sections read
sources.locator: Methods (55-63); Background (64-77); Guidance for Chemoprophylaxis / Household Contacts / Child Care Contacts (177-188)
sources.supports: US household prophylaxis criteria depend on underimmunized young children or immunocompromised minors in the household; these differ from UKHSA 2024. The page distinguishes disease treatment from carriage clearance.
sources.limits: The old assertion that non-b secondary transmission has not been documented is superseded by the 2025 CDC overview. Do not reproduce it. Vaccine products/schedules and professional regimens need current local verification.
sources.upstream: AAP Red Book 2012 cited for contact recommendations; systematic independence from UK evidence not established. Same CDC authoring family as cdc-hi-2025.

categories.title: Enteroviral meningitis

mece.reason: Same syndrome recognition and emergency pathway; limited named-virus transmission, host and treatment additions fit existing sections. A new article would duplicate most fourteen dimensions.
mece.exclusions: Do not map generic enterovirus infection, hand-foot-mouth disease, encephalitis, parechovirus or separately classified neonatal disease to this leaf.

fourteen_dimension_gaps.summary: Add explicit named enterovirus branch; viral overview alone does not allocate this scope.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.causes_risks: Add stool/secretions/hand and surface transmission and age context.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.red_flags: Reuse canonical emergency signs; avoid making fever mandatory based on a childhood enterovirus checklist.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.care: Explain confirmed mild-case discharge versus suspected meningitis; deterioration after prior review still needs reassessment.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.diagnosis: Name enterovirus testing within CSF work-up; do not equate stool positivity with proved meningitis.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.differentials: Separate enteroviral meningitis from encephalitis and ordinary enterovirus illness; preserve bacterial exclusion pathway.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.treatment: Allocate supportive treatment to the confirmed enterovirus branch; retain admission for severe/high-risk illness.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.medications: Prevent readers from applying herpes antiviral language to enterovirus; no routine specific antiviral regimen validated here.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.diet: Reuse assessed-case hydration advice; no separate enterovirus diet claim needed.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.daily_care: Add nappy/toilet hygiene and contaminated-surface cleaning; no new home scoring scheme.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.special_populations: Allocate young infants/immunocompromised risk; exact neonatal treatment remains outside this leaf package.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.prognosis_followup: Avoid guaranteed recovery deadline; persistence/deterioration requires individual reassessment.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.complications: Keep CNS complications distinct from wider enterovirus manifestations; no frequency estimates validated.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.prevention: Target hand hygiene and reduced secretion/stool exposure; omit global no-vaccine assertion.

minimum_additions: One named-enterovirus explanation spanning summary, causes and diagnosis.
One conditional supportive-care paragraph separating assessed mild cases from serious illness.
One hygiene paragraph plus scope-specific host and follow-up qualifications; inherit existing applicable common sections without duplicating them.

categories.title: Meningitis due to Haemophilus influenzae

mece.reason: Core bacterial meningitis pathway is already present. Add H. influenzae scope and a qualified Hib public-health branch, avoiding a duplicate general article.
mece.exclusions: This leaf is broader than Hib. Do not claim whole-leaf completion from b-serotype evidence alone; epiglottitis, bacteremia without meningitis and separate neonatal categories are outside this mapping.

fourteen_dimension_gaps.summary: Explicitly separate H. influenzae species scope from Hib subset and influenza virus.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.causes_risks: Allocate respiratory transmission, carriage and host risk to the named pathogen; do not generalize Hib epidemiology to all strains.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.red_flags: Reuse canonical urgent bacterial-meningitis signs; no new pathogen-specific diagnostic symptom claimed.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.care: Add prompt contact with treating/public-health team after confirmed Hib; avoid telling every household to self-medicate.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.diagnosis: Explain culture/PCR and why serotype matters for public-health action.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.differentials: Distinguish b serotype from non-b/nontypeable disease and influenza virus; syndrome still requires clinical testing.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.treatment: Common urgent inpatient antibacterial pathway can be reused; pathogen-specific regimen remains unverified by this package.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.medications: Separate acute treatment from prophylaxis/carriage clearance; do not add rifampin dose or universal household instruction.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.diet: No distinct diet claim needed; common nutrition support applies conditionally.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.daily_care: Add contact assessment and vaccination-record preparation alongside existing discharge care.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.special_populations: Clarify underimmunized children and immunocompromised hosts; elderly non-b disease not erased by childhood Hib framing.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.prognosis_followup: Reuse bacterial hearing/neurodevelopment follow-up after applicability review; no new absolute risk percentage.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.complications: Existing hearing/neurologic complications apply but require claim allocation; no new numerical prognostic estimate.
fourteen_dimension_gaps.prevention: Add Hib-only vaccine scope; jurisdiction-dependent contact management, with non-b advice individualized.

minimum_additions: Add species-versus-serotype scope and serotyping explanation.
Replace potential implication that only meningococcal contacts merit assessment with separate, carefully qualified Hib contact branch.
State local public-health advice determines prophylaxis and vaccination; retain general acute bacterial care without unsupported drug detail.
